stem: A researcher is studying renal hemodynamics in an experimental animal.  Manipulation of a single parameter leads to an immediate decrease in renal plasma flow and an increase in the filtration fraction before any compensatory responses occur.  Which of the following interventions most likely produced these findings?​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​​​​‌​​​‌‌
explanation:
Renal plasma flow (RPF) is the volume of plasma delivered to the kidneys per unit time, whereas glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is the volume filtered from the glomerular capillaries into Bowman space per unit time.  The filtration fraction (FF) is the proportion of renal plasma flow that undergoes filtration:

FF = GFR/RPF

Filtration is driven primarily by glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure and opposed by glomerular capillary oncotic pressure and Bowman space hydrostatic pressure.  Changes in afferent and efferent arteriolar resistance affect both plasma flow and glomerular capillary pressure, thereby altering GFR and filtration fraction.

Efferent arteriolar constriction increases resistance to blood leaving the glomerulus.  This decreases RPF while increasing glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure, which favors filtration.  With moderate constriction, GFR increases despite reduced plasma flow; therefore, a greater proportion of the delivered plasma is filtered, and filtration fraction increases.

Severe efferent constriction markedly reduces RPF.  As filtration removes water from the reduced plasma supply, proteins become more concentrated within the glomerular capillaries.  The resulting increase in glomerular capillary oncotic pressure opposes filtration and can decrease GFR despite the elevated hydrostatic pressure.  However, filtration fraction generally remains increased: although less fluid is filtered per minute, it represents a greater proportion of the reduced plasma flow.

(Choice A)  Afferent arteriolar constriction restricts blood entering the glomerulus, decreasing both RPF and glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure.  GFR also decreases, and filtration fraction remains approximately unchanged.  Sustained renal hypoperfusion can activate of the renin-angiotensin system (a compensatory response excluded by the stem); angiotensin II preferentially constricts the efferent arteriole, maintaining glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure and preserving GFR relative to the reduced RPF (thereby increasing filtration fraction).

(Choice C)  Afferent arteriolar dilation increases plasma delivery and glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure.  Both RPF and GFR increase, with relatively little change in filtration fraction.

(Choice D)  Efferent arteriolar dilation allows blood to leave the glomerulus more readily, increasing RPF while decreasing glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure and GFR.  Filtration fraction therefore decreases.

(Choice E)  Ureteral obstruction increases hydrostatic pressure upstream in the tubules and Bowman space, opposing filtration and decreasing GFR.  Before secondary vascular responses occur, RPF is relatively unchanged, so filtration fraction decreases.

Educational objective:Efferent arteriolar constriction decreases renal plasma flow while increasing glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure, thereby increasing the filtration fraction (GFR/RPF).  GFR increases with moderate constriction but can decrease with severe constriction as glomerular capillary oncotic pressure rises.​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​​​​‌​​​‌‌
